jobs.title: Sr. Manager/Director FP&A
jobs.description:
ABOUT LUMILENS

At Lumilens we are building the critical photonics infrastructure that powers tomorrow’s AI supercomputing. From chip-to-chip optical interconnects to scalable photonic engines, Lumilens is unlocking a new era of computing - faster, cooler, and massively more efficient. 
 
We’re a well-funded startup backed by Mayfield and led by veterans who’ve built and scaled some of the most transformative technologies in the industry. At Lumilens, we’re developing high-speed photonics products purpose-built to power the future of AI infrastructure and high-performance computing. 
 
This isn’t incremental innovation, it’s a ground-floor opportunity to rethink the optical layer from the silicon up. You’ll work alongside a team of world-class engineers solving some of the hardest challenges in scaling optical systems. Every line of code, every design decision, every breakthrough you help deliver will shape the infrastructure of tomorrow. 
 
If you're looking for mission, momentum, and the chance to make an outsized impact, jump on the rocket ship. We’re just getting started.

The Role

This role is at the core of Lumilens’ global FP&A delivery from Bangalore, partnering closely with R&D and business leaders to drive financial planning, business partnership, and decision support. As a member of the India Leadership team, this leader will also collectively act as country controller for the India entity, helping build financial discipline, scalable planning processes, and strong operating visibility in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

Key Responsibilities

 - Own the annual operating plan, quarterly forecasts, and monthly variance analysis for the assigned SBU or function.

 - Partner with business leaders to drive financial discipline, evaluate investments, and track operational KPIs.

 - Build driver-based financial models across revenue, gross margin, operating expenses, and capital expenditures.

 - Lead pricing analysis, customer and product profitability reviews, and unit economics assessments.

 - Drive India R&D expense planning, tracking, and project-level variance management.

 - Act as country controller for the India entity, including support for statutory close, audit, tax filings, and transfer pricing.

 - Support board reporting, investor relations materials, and earnings preparation in support of a US listing.

 - Drive scenario planning, sensitivity analysis, and strategic financial reviews to support key business decisions.

 - Coach analysts and mentor junior team members while helping build a strong finance organization in India.

Required Qualifications

 - CPA, CFA, or MBA required.

 - 10–15 years of FP&A or strategic finance experience.

 - Technology industry FP&A or strategic finance experience, or an engineering degree combined with an MBA.

 - Ability to operate effectively in a startup environment with ambiguity and limited structure, including building processes from scratch without established playbooks.

 - Strong financial modeling, scenario analysis, and business partnering capabilities.

 - Proven ability to influence senior business leaders through data-driven insights and sound financial judgment.

 - Advanced financial modeling skills and comfort working with large datasets.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience in technology, hardware, semiconductor, or FMCG industries.

 - Manufacturing cost accounting exposure.

 - A track record of building and developing finance teams and processes from scratch.

 - US MNC experience as a controller or senior finance leader within a US-headquartered multinational.

What We Offer

 - A highly visible leadership role with the opportunity to shape financial and operational decisions in a fast-scaling deep-tech manufacturing environment.

 - The chance to work at the intersection of finance, operations, and advanced photonics technology—where your analysis directly influences investment, margin, and scale.

 - Competitive compensation commensurate with experience, along with comprehensive health benefits.

 - Meaningful exposure to cross-functional and global leadership teams across Singapore, Thailand, Canada, and the United States.

 - Professional growth and development opportunities, including the ability to build processes, strengthen systems, and help define the next chapter of operations finance at Lumilens.

 - A collaborative, ambitious environment where experienced operators can make an outsized impact and help build something category-defining from the ground up.



*Lumilens is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, gender, identity, orientation, veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Sr. Manager/Director FP&A
jobs.description:
Role Overview

Senior FP&A lead in California with a tightly scoped operational mandate: own FP&A for the US R&D lab, lead revenue management for the Hyperscaler customer segment, and act as US country controller for the US-listed entity.

Key Responsibilities

 - Own US R&D lab budgeting, forecasting, project-level cost tracking, and capex planning

 - Lead revenue management for Hyperscaler customers — pricing, contract economics, deal review, revenue recognition, customer profitability

 - Act as US country controller — own US entity close, statutory reporting, tax filings, audit support, and internal controls

 - Partner with US sales leadership on revenue forecasting, commission planning, and deal economics for Hyperscaler accounts

 - Support board reporting and investor relations content tied to US operations and the Hyperscaler segment

 - Drive long-range planning for US R&D investment and Hyperscaler revenue strategy

 - Drive automation across US FP&A and controllership processes

Required Qualifications (all mandatory)

 - CPA / CFA / MBA

 - 10-15 years of FP&A or strategic finance experience

 - Tech industry FP&A / strategic finance experience OR engineering degree combined with an MBA

 - Ability to operate in a startup, unstructured, ambiguous environment

 - Strong operational FP&A experience — manufacturing, supply chain, or hardware cost analysis

 - Proven business partnering with operations and commercial leaders

 - Advanced financial modeling; comfort with large datasets

Preferred Qualifications

 - Technology / hardware / semiconductor / FMCG industry experience

 - Manufacturing cost accounting exposure

 - Track record of building and developing finance teams and processes from scratch.

 - US MNC experience — controller or senior finance leader inside a US-headquartered multinational

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager
jobs.description:
SENIOR PROGRAM MANAGER – NPI

About Lumilens

 

At Lumilens, we are building critical photonics infrastructure powering tomorrow’s AI supercomputing. From chip-to-chip optical interconnects to scalable photonic engines, Lumilens is unlocking a new era of computing—faster, cooler, and massively more efficient. Join our collaborative team to shape the future of high-speed optical connectivity.

 

Position Overview

 

We are seeking an experienced Senior Program Manager specializing in New Product Introduction (NPI). The ideal candidate will have over 15 years of experience in the NPI domain, preferably within the switching and networking industry. This leader will demonstrate proven expertise managing programs from early prototyping through pilot manufacturing, with solid exposure to hardware development fundamentals and manufacturing processes.

 

Responsibilities

 

 - Lead complex NPI programs from concept through prototyping and into pilot manufacturing

 - Manage program end-to-end, wall-to-wall, ensuring all phases from initiation to closure are delivered successfully

 - Work extensively with cross-functional teams spread across geographies to ensure alignment and timely delivery

 - Collaborate with engineering, operations, and manufacturing teams to ensure milestones are achieved on schedule

 - Drive planning and execution of early hardware prototyping and transition to scalable manufacturing

 - Manage program risk, develop mitigation plans, and communicate status to stakeholders

 - Ensure robust design transfer processes and readiness for manufacturing

 - Maintain detailed documentation and program tracking tools

 - Champion continuous improvement in program management practices

 

Required Qualifications

 

 - More than 15 years of program management experience in the NPI space, preferably in switching and networking domains

 - Demonstrated proficiency in managing programs end-to-end, wall-to-wall, across all project phases

 - Proven experience working with teams distributed across different global geographies

 - Excellent track record of leading programs from prototyping through pilot manufacturing

 - Strong understanding of hardware design, development processes, and manufacturing fundamentals

 - Proficiency in project management tools, methodologies, and communication

 - Collaborative mindset with strong organizational, analytical, and leadership skills

 - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering or a related field

 

Why Join Lumilens?

 

 - Work at the forefront of AI, networking, and optical semiconductor technology

 - Collaborative and innovative environment

 - Opportunities for career growth

 - Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package

 

Lumilens is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or any other protected characteristic.

jobs.title: General Manager, Singapore
jobs.description:
ABOUT LUMILENS

At Lumilens we are building the critical photonics infrastructure that powers tomorrow’s AI supercomputing. From chip-to-chip optical interconnects to scalable photonic engines, Lumilens is unlocking a new era of computing - faster, cooler, and massively more efficient.

We’re a well-funded startup backed by Mayfield and led by veterans who’ve built and scaled some of the most transformative technologies in the industry. At Lumilens, we’re developing high-speed photonics products purpose-built to power the future of AI infrastructure and high-performance computing.

This isn’t incremental innovation, it’s a ground-floor opportunity to rethink the optical layer from the silicon up. You’ll work alongside a team of world-class engineers solving some of the hardest challenges in scaling optical systems. Every line of code, every design decision, every breakthrough you help deliver will shape the infrastructure of tomorrow.

If you're looking for mission, momentum, and the chance to make an outsized impact, jump on the rocket ship. We’re just getting started.



POSITION OVERVIEW

We are seeking a seasoned General Manager to lead end-to end operational execution as the company scales its next generation optical transceiver and photonics products from NPI into high volume global manufacturing.

As GM you will serve as the single-threaded owner for delivery, cost, quality, and capacity across Lumilens’ manufacturing ecosystem. You’ll work closely with OEM partners, critical component suppliers, and internal engineering and planning teams. This role requires a rare blend of technical depth, operational rigor, supplier leadership, and strategic judgment to translate innovation into reliable, scalable and world-class production.



DUTIES / RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Own end-to-end operational execution for Lumilens’ product portfolio (800G / 1.6T optical modules and beyond), with full accountability for on-time delivery, cost, quality, and scalable ramp-up.

2. Serve as the ultimate escalation authority for all production, yield, capacity, quality, and supplier-related issues to ensure rapid resolution

3. Translate customer demand and revenue targets into executable build plans, capacity commitments, and supply strategies.

4. Lead and govern Lumilens’ global manufacturing ecosystem, including EMS/ODM partners, OSATs, fabs, and critical sub-tier suppliers.

5. Drive capacity planning, ramp readiness, and risk mitigation across multiple sites.

6. Negotiate and manage commercial agreements, including pricing, capacity reservations, long-term supply commitments, and cost-down initiatives with key vendors.

7. Establish and maintain robust dual-sourcing strategies, second-source qualifications, and supplier contingency plans to ensure supply continuity.

8. Own COGS performance, BOM cost reductions, PPV tracking, and long-term cost-down roadmaps.

9. Act as an operational partner to Product and Hardware Engineering teams, to ensure seamless alignment between design intent and manufacturing execution.

10. Embed design-for-manufacturability (DFM/DFX) principles early in the NPI lifecycle to enable scalable, high-yield production.

11. Build scalable operating cadence, including weekly build reviews, QBRs with suppliers, and executive dashboards.

12. Implement and mature processes for demand planning, S&OP, supplier scorecards, and quality management.

13. Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing team across operations, supply chain, planning, and quality.

14. Create clarity of ownership, accountability, and decision rights across functions.



QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Progressive leadership experience in operations, manufacturing, or supply chain roles within hardware, deep-tech, or advanced electronics environments.

 - Proven track record of scaling products from NPI through high-volume manufacturing, including ownership of yield, quality, cost, and delivery.

 - Strong technical foundation in optics, semiconductors, electronics manufacturing, or closely related industries; experience with optical transceivers, data-centre hardware, or high-speed networking products is preferred

 - Bachelor’s degree or advanced technical degree/ MBA in electrical engineering, Industrial Engineering, Physics, or a related field.

 - Deep hands-on expertise in manufacturing process development, yield analysis, root-cause problem solving, and implementation of corrective actions.

 - Strong commercial acumen, with experience negotiating pricing, capacity commitments, long-term supply agreements, and cost-reduction initiatives.

 - In-depth knowledge of quality management systems (QMS), reliability testing, and quality standards applicable to high-volume electronics and optics manufacturing.

 - Experience working across Asia-based manufacturing hubs, including Taiwan, Thailand, China, and Vietnam. Experience working in Singapore will be an advantage.

 - Resourceful and analytical problem-solver, capable of managing multiple concurrent programs and priorities in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.

 - Proven ability to operate effectively within geographically distributed, cross-functional teams, partnering closely with engineering, quality, finance, and commercial functions.

 - Strong English communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to present to senior stakeholders and mentor and develop teams.

 - Willingness and ability to travel internationally as required.



Equal Employment Opportunity

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, religious creed, sex, national origin, ancestry, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, gender, gender expression, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws and regulations.
